title: Your lifting program SUCKS! (Hypertrophy Q&A / Program review)
summary: Three-hour hypertrophy Q&A stream where NH answers rapid-fire chat questions (exercise picks, injuries, frequency, natural limits) and then screen-shares and critiques about a dozen subscriber programs. Recurring themes: superset non-competing muscles, start with compounds, avoid redundancy and excess volume, use evolving set/rep ranges, and train as little time as needed for results.
claims: Split squats are his favourite leg movement because their stimulus-to-fatigue ratio is excellent; load them with a safety squat bar or similar rather than dumbbells
Moving split squats from dumbbells to a safety squat bar let him add 80 lb; the balance demand had made him unknowingly go light
His big three for massive legs: split squats, RDLs and heel-elevated squats; RDLs put huge mass on the posterior chain
A stubborn chest needs a pressing movement you personally connect with; some people feel every press in shoulders or triceps
A split squat goes straight up and down while a lunge moves the body forward dynamically; he prefers split squats for hypertrophy
He now squats in flat shoes and sees no difference; he only keeps Olympic lifting shoes for high-bar squats
Torso/limbs splits risk imbalance because torso work already trains limbs and people overemphasise the torso; he prefers an upper/lower gentleman split with some compounds even on arm days
To fill the hollow above the clavicle build the traps; short clavicles are an advantage because there is less space to fill
For biceps tendinitis, avoid supinated curls for a while, stay pronated, then rehab supination gradually; the cause is often presses, dips or pull-ups
On anti-inflammatories and painkillers, avoid max singles, stick to high reps and prioritise recovery because pain signals are masked
Hammer curls are not mandatory but some neutral/pronated work is needed to thicken the brachioradialis
Barbell rows are an overall posterior-chain builder, not a replacement for RDLs, and rank low for upper back versus pulls where the upper back is the limiting factor
A 10x10 is sandbagging, not high intensity; 4-6 hard sets per muscle per session is high volume you can still push to the wall
The bodybuilding middle back is mostly mid/low traps and rhomboids; he hits it best with Kroc rows, torso fairly vertical, elbow high, rowing toward the body
Train the tibialis twice a week to start, then build to three times
He was repeatedly injured squatting with a wide, toes-out stance copied from others; a narrow stance with feet forward made his legs bigger, stronger and his knees pain-free
Dumbbell deadlifts teach novices to use their legs; after ~2 years of them in his bedroom his first barbell deadlift was 225 lb
On dumbbell rows, hip shifts or knee bends to heave the weight are bad momentum; a slight torso shift to finish a hard rep is acceptable, and stop when reps get dirty
The stretch-focused trend is contrarian content; he believes the concentric builds more muscle than the eccentric and proposes a partner-removes-the-negative experiment to prove it
He avoids arm wrestling because elbow injury risk is high and his arms took too long to build
If you can only train Saturday, Sunday and Wednesday: upper, lower, then full body
He has replaced bench press entirely with ring push-ups and dips and is doing better for it
Farmer walks without straps build grip and with straps build massive traps
On a bulk eat foods you enjoy that fit your macros, and avoid foods that bloat you
Adjustable dumbbells are only worth buying if you use dumbbells a lot
He does not lock out overhead presses because nothing happens at lockout unless you compete
He sells any home equipment he doesn't use weekly; his last purchase was a tibialis raise station used three times a week
He prefers strongman to powerlifting as a more complete sport with better physiques and no longer watches the Olympia
He joined a commercial gym because home-gym limits explain his lagging triceps and shoulders; Smith presses and cable lateral raises finally let him feel his delts
Lock out dips for stability and safety at the top, not for hypertrophy
Lateral raises above parallel add nothing; standardise range at parallel and load that part
Lu raises are fine for shoulder health or rehab but poor for hypertrophy because light plates limit loading
He trains neck every lower-body day, twice a week; neck rotations are unnecessary except for athletes where injuries happen
Top front-body upper exercises: dips, chin/pull-ups, forearm isolation, ab isolation, then a military press
Dips and pull-ups are S-tier; overloading weighted dips changed his mind and grew his triceps
Rotate lateral raise variations (cable, dumbbell) to keep progressing
His arms went from 18 to about 18.4 in over ~2 years; 19 in might take 2-3 more years
He warms up for dips with three heavy military press sets and loses no dip performance
With only two days a week, do upper/lower and sneak isolation into 10-15 minute gaps during the week
His sessions last 2-2.5 hours door to door, warm-ups included
He keeps taking MSM because his joints suffer quickly when he stops
His years of chasing numbers were his worst: constant injuries and poor gains
Rest-pause with 10-15 s between mini-sets works; don't overdo it
Back extensions count as a hip hinge; if you progress them that's enough
Leg press is a perfectly fine leg builder despite squat supremacists
Lifting alongside BJJ should be minimal and aimed at surviving the sport, protecting shoulders and knees, not maximal hypertrophy
To avoid wrist pain on bench, stack the joint instead of letting the wrist bend back
Military press is a plateau machine because it is unstable; Smith press, single-arm or seated dumbbell press progress better
Lifters who chase big-three strength often stay skinny-fat; the powerlifting-builds-physique idea is a meme and they should pivot
Every pec press trains the upper chest; incline press is a deltoid movement before an upper-chest one, and emphasis comes from elbow angle and sensation
Lower-body days need 3-4 movements; upper days 6-8, up to 10
Low-rep compounds get 2-3 sets, never more
His first-year YouTube programs were too high in volume and frequency
To get a partner training, frame it as time together and start very easy (bar box squats, assisted split squats, 5 lb dumbbell press); results become the motivation
Most women look better heavier with more muscle; media made them obsess over the scale
An 8-16 rep range is too wide on hammer curls and keeps you on one weight too long; 6-12 is the widest he'd allow
Stop doing AMRAP on movements just to build capacity; if a movement can be loaded (neck with a harness, abs), load it
An upper body built only from compounds with no arm isolation leads to imbalance
Redundant thin days should be compressed (5 days to 4 or 3); spend as little time in the gym as possible for the result
Many bodybuilders write good lower days but neglect their upper days
Bench press supersetted with pullovers is his favourite superset
Avoid convoluted multi-word exercise variants copied from influencers; use normal movements and do less
Fat grips do not replace forearm isolation
Cutting pullovers to two sets because more lat work follows is smart volume management
Dips late in a day after pressing and triceps are fine as bodyweight AMRAP, but weighted dips belong earlier
Use high reps (12-18) on forearm moves like pronation twists; rest-pause gains more extra reps the higher the rep range
Weighted pull-ups work best around 5-8 reps; 6-10 is the upper limit
Heavy supersets require built-up work capacity but then allow lots of quality volume in less time
Preacher curls at 5-10 only suit experienced lifters; others use 8-12; newcomers to skullcrushers should use 10-15 to habituate tendons
Cable hammer curls with the cable behind you allow a strong stretch
Front squats suit low reps (4-6) because heavier loads keep the front rack from limiting
Don't superset RDLs with heavy shrugs: a fatigued upper back limits the posterior chain
Giant sets belong at the end of a session and should mostly be isolation, for time efficiency
Training lateral raises once a week is enough; two or three times often hinders progression
Maingaining at 11-12% body fat is perfectly doable
Properly done upright rows are a good side-delt isolation
Swinging on hanging knee raises means losing control of the negative and skipping the stretch
Direct brachioradialis work isn't vital; cross-body hammer curls suffice
JM presses are polarising, but many report they rescued their elbows
Overhead extensions are not the only way to train the triceps long head
Dumbbell pullovers supplement but cannot replace pull-ups or pulldowns
Sport-specific training like arm wrestling is in its infancy and full of nonsense such as grippers
He doubts natural 21 in arms; 19-20 in naturals are plausible, old measurements were inflated, and fat makes 20 in easy
You cannot save a friend who doesn't want saving; draw him out through activities he already enjoys
Busy, sleep-deprived lifters don't need high frequency; full body twice a week is excellent and his Silver Era program at 2-3 days beats a demanding PPL
Recurring neck/upper-back numbness from stuck nerves is helped by training and stretching the neck
Bar pull-ups beat ring pull-ups; rings are less stable and just more portable
Slow controlled neck curls with a 45 lb plate mean good neck strength
For bloating, find and eliminate trigger foods (dairy, red meat, gluten, oats, pasta)
Blue-collar workers can grow but should train less often, with more intensity and less volume
His programs use an evolving set range: once the first set tops the rep range, add a set; at the top set count add weight and drop back
He takes only creatine, MSM and protein; test boosters are a scam
He is anti-stimulant and takes no pre-workout
Progress hanging leg raises by switching to Roman chair knee raises holding a dumbbell
Spider curls after incline curls are done fatigued; rotate them week to week instead
Two sets on an intense movement like incline curls is enough
Back-off sets of high-bar squats aren't needed if legs aren't a priority; two sets suffice
A different rep range on the same lift counts as a variation
Leg press at 6 reps is unrealistic; use 10-15
If you can do 6-12 bodyweight pull-ups, add weight and use a lower rep range
Supersets work in a gym if practical, e.g. incline press and incline curls on the same bench
6-10 reps is too low for isolation; use 8-12 or 10-15
He dislikes hip thrusts because there is almost always a better option
Superset non-competing muscles (leg press with neck curls) to avoid fatiguing the same muscle
Keep evolving set ranges within one set (2-3, 3-4); a 1-4 range stalls progress, especially on compounds
Leg raises are best replaced by knee raises: easier to load and control
Start with compounds; open with isolation only if that muscle is a weak point
Most bodybuilders could cut volume 20-30% and get the same results
Lower days are simple: one heavy posterior chain lift, some quad work; split squats spare the low back after RDLs
Never open a day with shrugs before weighted pull-ups; do the most demanding movement first
Avoid the same isolation on consecutive days; give it 48 hours
Bodyweight-only training usually lacks traps, side delts, forearms and posterior chain; add them
Weighted dips plus French press twice a week will wreck your elbows
Calisthenics lifters should do pull-ups at least twice a week
Hinges suffice for hamstrings but leg curls are free volume if available
Deadlift is not the best hypertrophy lift; bench-only pressing invites plateaus and shoulder issues, so add a vertical press, bench variants and face pulls
A long-neglected muscle has poor work capacity and recovery; it isn't stubborn, you just haven't trained it
Full body twice a week should rotate variations rather than repeat an identical day, to prevent overuse injuries
Bench press and weighted dips on the same day are redundant; pick one and rotate
For boxers bench isn't functional; prefer ring or deficit push-ups, face pulls for posture, lunges and trap-bar deadlifts
Athletes need minimalist programs that carry over to their sport
He adds weight to dips about every two weeks and reps otherwise; a year of this took him to four extra plates
Stalled progress usually means poor recovery, low effort, bad programming or a bad lift; straight-bar OHP stalled while Smith press keeps climbing
Tall lifters don't gain strength slower but visual change takes longer, roughly 4-5 years versus 2
Most people set incline bench too steep; lower it, which also lets a vertical press be added
After 6 months off, restart with 1-2 submaximal sets and let muscle memory work
He does Bulgarian split squats for 8-12 reps
Use a pronated grip on barbell rows; supinated grip risks the biceps
Small wrists don't stop you from building big forearms
After a back tweak, reintroduce hyperextensions gradually and stay active
Frequency is a tool for fitting volume; intermediates need at least 3 days, 4 is his favourite and sustainable for life
He went from 7 to 6 to 5 training days a week and still progresses
He does 2-3 sets of 3-5 reps on dips per week, no back-off sets
Start weighting pull-ups and dips after 10 clean pull-ups and 15 clean dips, adding 5-10 lb
End each session with a little energy left; that shows good programming
Train obliques with dumbbell twists and suitcase deadlifts
Full body three times a week is one of the best templates
He will someday cut to 180-190 lb to compete
Naturals lose muscle slowly and regain it quickly
Over 3-4 years his programming moved to less volume, less frequency, more intensity
Adding junk food to a bulk is okay if you're very skinny
